newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says firm against rebel "blackmail".
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says firm against rebel "blackmail".

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Tuesday he would remain firm in the three-week-old hostage crisis in Lima and would not give in to what he called "terrorist" blackmail.
"We maintain a firm position of not giving in to blackmail from the terrorists," Fujimori told reporters.

"I think that in the situation in which we find ourselves there are principles that should be respected, although at the same time we must look for a way out of the crisis," Fujimori added in brief comments to reporters as he left Government Palace. He did not elaborate.

The president had previously spoken in public only twice about the crisis that started when Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Dec. 17.

The rebels, who hold 74 hostages, are demanding the government free all their 400-plus jailed comrades. Fujimori has rejected the demand and has said he will only look for a "way out" that does not use force if the guerrillas release all their hostages and laid down their arms.

Progress toward a solution seemed at a standstill Tuesday. After freeing more than 430 hostages, the rebels have not released any captives for six days and the government negotiator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo, has not reentered the building since a first meeting Dec. 28 with the guerrillas.
